text:
alice: Heads-up — ap-southeast GPU fleet showing sustained p99 tail on hosted slices this morning. Dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/gpu/ap-southeast · top noisy tenant looks like `summit-ml` (KV-cache regen + heavy egress). Thinking about a short carveout: a small subnet/rack pool for heavy-egress tenants with stricter routing/egress shaping to protect usual multi-tenant slices. Any objections?
ben: Can you share the key metrics? how bad is the impact on casual tenants (p50/p95/p99)? also cost delta for carveout? :thinking_face:
achar: p50 ~ 12ms, p95 ~ 45ms, p99 jumps to 420-650ms depending on burst windows. cc @ben there's a clear correlation between high KV-cache miss rate and p99 spikes. egress throughput for summit-ml peaks ~6-8Gbps sustained during jobs.
chloe: I like the subnet carveout idea but prefer a routing constraint first: schedule heavy-egress tasks to labeled racks (egress-capable) and apply nic-policing + token-bucket at L3. That lets us measure improvement without fully committing to dedicated capacity.
ben: +1 for stepwise approach. What's the simplest experiment? carve 2 racks, add label, attach egress-shaper 10Gbps per tenant, run for 48h?
achloe: Yep. Plan: 1) carve two racks in ap-southeast as `egress-shield-001` 2) add node-labels: `egress_shield=true` 3) scheduler affinity rule for tenants with >3Gbps 4) egress qdisc policing: `tc qdisc replace dev eth0 root handle 1: tbf rate 10gbit burst 32k latency 400ms` 5) enable KV-cache warmup on those racks. Quick snippet to create label on nodes: ```bash
# mark nodes
for node in $(kubectl get nodes -l rack=ap-southeast-2 -o name | head -n 6); do
  kubectl label $node egress_shield=true --overwrite
done
# scheduler tweak
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata:
  name: egress-shield
value: 1000
EOF
```
devops-bot: alert: ap-southeast/gpu-pool p99 > 500ms for 12m — noisy-tenant correlation tag="summit-ml". Suggested runbook: create temporary carveout and route heavy egress.
alice: I put together a quick cost estimate: two racks (~8 GPUs each) reserved on-demand -> incremental infra + network egress ~ $3k/week if fully saturated. If we go fractional (soft carveout) cost is just scheduling overhead. I'm happy to sign off on the 48h canary.
ben: Who owns the rollout and rollback? need SRE on-call, chloe to run the node labeling, alice to monitor dashboards, and me for cost tracking. Also add an automatic fallback policy to move tenants back if p95 for normal slices increases.
achloe: I'll run labeling + qdisc tonight at 02:00 UTC; will instrument dashboards and start canary routing. Rollback command: `kubectl label nodes -l egress_shield=true egress_shield-` and remove scheduler affinity.
alice: Please also add a remote trace hook to collect KV-cache hit/miss every 5m. If p99 for shared slices doesn't drop by >= 35% after 6h, abort.
ben: +1. chloe ping me when finished and I'll run the cost accounting job.
chloe: doing it now, logging to #eng-infra. will post short summary and raw traces when the canary stabilizes. :thumbsup:
devops-bot: info: canary started by chloe at 5967890200, assigned run_id=canary-egress-5967. Good luck!
alice: thanks team. if this reduces noisy neighbor spikes we can bake an automatic scheduler rule to pre-assign heavy-egress tenants during peak windows.
ben: FYI we should capture the cleanup steps in runbook afterwards.
chloe: noted — will update runbook with `egress_shield` playbook entries and cost numbers.
alice: ok closing thread for now; follow-ups will be posted to the canary run thread.
